# Async Timeout and Cancellation Usage Guide

Source: https://github.com/utkarsh-cpu/cpp-agentic-framework/blob/master/docs/AsyncTimeoutUsage.md

# Async Timeout and Cancellation Usage Guide

This document explains how to use the timeout and cancellation features implemented in the C++ Agentic Framework.

## Overview

The framework now provides comprehensive timeout and cancellation support for async operations through several key components:

- **CancellationToken**: Thread-safe cancellation signaling
- **TimeoutPolicy**: Configurable timeout policies for different operation types
- **AsyncTimeout**: Template functions for executing operations with timeout
- **AsyncNode Integration**: Enhanced AsyncNode with timeout and cancellation support

## Core Components

### 1. CancellationToken

The `CancellationToken` provides a thread-safe way to signal cancellation to long-running operations.

```cpp
#include "BaseNode/CancellationToken.h"

// Create a cancellation token source
CancellationTokenSource token_source;

// Check if cancellation was requested
if (token_source.token().is_cancellation_requested()) {
    // Handle cancellation
}

// Throw if cancellation was requested
token_source.token().throw_if_cancellation_requested();

// Register a callback for when cancellation occurs
token_source.token().register_callback([]() {
    std::cout << "Operation was cancelled!" << std::endl;
});

// Cancel the operation
token_source.cancel();
```

### 2. TimeoutPolicy

`TimeoutPolicy` allows you to define timeout behavior for different types of operations.

```cpp
#include "BaseNode/TimeoutPolicy.h"

// Use predefined policies
auto fast_policy = TimeoutPolicy::for_operation(TimeoutPolicy::OperationType::FAST_OPERATION);
auto normal_policy = TimeoutPolicy::for_operation(TimeoutPolicy::OperationType::NORMAL_OPERATION);
auto batch_policy = TimeoutPolicy::for_operation(TimeoutPolicy::OperationType::BATCH_OPERATION);

// Create custom policy
auto custom_policy = TimeoutPolicy(
    std::chrono::seconds(30),    // timeout duration
    true,                        // enable cancellation
    std::chrono::seconds(5)      // cleanup timeout
);

// Register named policies
TimeoutPolicyRegistry::instance().register_policy("my_policy", custom_policy);
```

### 3. Execute with Timeout

The framework provides template functions for executing operations with timeout support.

```cpp
#include "BaseNode/AsyncTimeout.h"

// Simple timeout execution
auto simple_work = [](int duration_seconds) -> std::string {
    std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::seconds(duration_seconds));
    return "Work completed";
};

try {
    auto result = execute_with_timeout(simple_work, std::chrono::seconds(5), 2);
    std::cout << "Result: " << result << std::endl;
} catch (const TimeoutException& e) {
    std::cout << "Operation timed out: " << e.what() << std::endl;
}

// Cancellation-aware execution
auto cancellable_work = [](const CancellationToken& token, int iterations) -> std::string {
    for (int i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
        token.throw_if_cancellation_requested();
        std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(100));
    }
    return "Cancellable work completed";
};

try {
    auto result = execute_with_timeout_and_cancellation(
        cancellable_work, 
        std::chrono::seconds(2), 
        50  // 50 iterations of 100ms each
    );
    std::cout << "Result: " << result << std::endl;
} catch (const TimeoutException& e) {
    std::cout << "Operation timed out: " << e.what() << std::endl;
} catch (const OperationCancelledException& e) {
    std::cout << "Operation was cancelled: " << e.what() << std::endl;
}
```

### 4. AsyncNode Integration

The `AsyncNode` class now supports timeout and cancellation through new methods.

```cpp
#include "AsyncNode/AsyncNode.h"

class MyAsyncNode : public AsyncNode {
public:
    std::future<std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData>> ExecAsync(std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> PrepRes) override {
        return std::async(std::launch::async, [this, PrepRes]() -> std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> {
            // Your async work here
            std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::seconds(2));
            return std::make_shared<StringData>("Work completed");
        });
    }

protected:
    std::future<std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData>> ExecAsyncWithCancellation(
        std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> PrepRes, const CancellationToken& token) override {
        
        return std::async(std::launch::async, [this, PrepRes, &token]() -> std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> {
            // Check for cancellation periodically
            for (int i = 0; i < 20; ++i) {
                token.throw_if_cancellation_requested();
                std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(100));
            }
            return std::make_shared<StringData>("Cancellable work completed");
        });
    }
};

// Usage
auto node = std::make_shared<MyAsyncNode>();
auto input_data = std::make_shared<StringData>("input");

// Execute with timeout
try {
    auto future = node->RunAsyncWithTimeout(input_data, std::chrono::seconds(5));
    auto result = future.get();
} catch (const TimeoutException& e) {
    std::cout << "Node execution timed out" << std::endl;
}

// Execute with policy
try {
    auto future = node->RunAsyncWithPolicy(input_data, "fast");
    auto result = future.get();
} catch (const TimeoutException& e) {
    std::cout << "Node execution timed out with fast policy" << std::endl;
}

// Execute with cancellation
CancellationTokenSource token_source;
try {
    auto future = node->RunAsyncWithCancellation(input_data, token_source.token());
    
    // Cancel after some time
    std::thread canceller([&token_source]() {
        std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::seconds(1));
        token_source.cancel();
    });
    
    auto result = future.get();
    canceller.join();
} catch (const OperationCancelledException& e) {
    std::cout << "Node execution was cancelled" << std::endl;
}
```

## Exception Types

The framework defines specific exception types for timeout and cancellation scenarios:

### TimeoutException

Thrown when an operation exceeds its timeout duration.

```cpp
try {
    // Some operation that might timeout
} catch (const TimeoutException& e) {
    std::cout << "Timeout: " << e.what() << std::endl;
    std::cout << "Duration: " << e.timeout_duration().count() << "ms" << std::endl;
    std::cout << "Category: " << static_cast<int>(e.category()) << std::endl;
}
```

### OperationCancelledException

Thrown when an operation is cancelled via a cancellation token.

```cpp
try {
    // Some cancellable operation
} catch (const OperationCancelledException& e) {
    std::cout << "Cancelled: " << e.what() << std::endl;
    std::cout << "Category: " << static_cast<int>(e.category()) << std::endl;
}
```

## Best Practices

### 1. Choose Appropriate Timeouts

- **Fast operations**: 1-5 seconds
- **Normal operations**: 30 seconds
- **Batch operations**: 5-15 minutes
- **Network operations**: 10-30 seconds

### 2. Implement Cancellation Checking

For long-running operations, check for cancellation regularly:

```cpp
auto long_running_work = [](const CancellationToken& token) {
    for (int i = 0; i < 1000; ++i) {
        // Check for cancellation every iteration
        token.throw_if_cancellation_requested();
        
        // Do some work
        std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(10));
    }
};
```

### 3. Handle Cleanup Properly

Always ensure proper cleanup in your async operations:

```cpp
class MyAsyncNode : public AsyncNode {
protected:
    void cleanup_resources() noexcept override {
        try {
            // Close file handles
            // Release network connections
            // Clear temporary buffers
            // Reset internal state
        } catch (...) {
            // Log error but don't propagate
        }
    }
};
```

### 4. Use Appropriate Policies

Register and use named policies for consistency:

```cpp
// At application startup
TimeoutPolicyRegistry::instance().register_policy(
    "database_query", 
    TimeoutPolicy(std::chrono::seconds(30), true, std::chrono::seconds(5))
);

TimeoutPolicyRegistry::instance().register_policy(
    "file_upload", 
    TimeoutPolicy(std::chrono::minutes(5), true, std::chrono::seconds(10))
);

// In your code
auto future = node->RunAsyncWithPolicy(data, "database_query");
```

## Testing

The framework includes comprehensive tests for timeout and cancellation functionality. Key test areas include:

- Basic timeout functionality
- Cancellation token behavior
- Timeout policy configuration
- Exception handling
- Integration with AsyncNode

## Limitations

1. **Thread Safety**: The current implementation has some threading complexity that may cause issues in certain scenarios.
2. **Cleanup Guarantees**: While cleanup is attempted, there's no guarantee that all resources will be cleaned up if a thread is forcibly terminated.
3. **Platform Dependencies**: Some timeout mechanisms may behave differently across platforms.

## Future Improvements

1. **Coroutine Support**: Integration with C++20 coroutines for better async programming
2. **Hierarchical Cancellation**: Support for parent-child cancellation relationships
3. **Progress Reporting**: Integration with progress reporting mechanisms
4. **Retry Policies**: Automatic retry with exponential backoff for failed operations

---

# Concurrency and Thread Safety Guide

Source: https://github.com/utkarsh-cpu/cpp-agentic-framework/blob/master/docs/CONCURRENCY_GUIDE.md

# Concurrency and Thread Safety Guide

## Table of Contents

1. [Overview](#overview)
2. [Thread Safety Guarantees](#thread-safety-guarantees)
3. [Synchronization Primitives](#synchronization-primitives)
4. [Async Programming Patterns](#async-programming-patterns)
5. [Cancellation and Timeouts](#cancellation-and-timeouts)
6. [Lock-Free Programming](#lock-free-programming)
7. [Common Pitfalls and Solutions](#common-pitfalls-and-solutions)
8. [Best Practices](#best-practices)

## Overview

The C++ Agentic Framework is designed with thread safety as a core principle. This guide explains the concurrency model, thread safety guarantees, and best practices for building high-performance concurrent applications.

### Concurrency Model

The framework uses a hybrid concurrency model:

1. **Shared-Nothing Architecture**: Each node processes data independently
2. **Immutable Data**: FrameworkData objects are immutable after construction
3. **Thread-Safe Operations**: All public APIs are thread-safe
4. **Async-First Design**: Built-in support for asynchronous operations

## Thread Safety Guarantees

### BaseNode Thread Safety

All BaseNode operations are thread-safe and can be called concurrently from multiple threads:

```cpp
#include "BaseNode/BaseNode.h"
#include <thread>
#include <vector>

class ThreadSafeExample {
public:
    void demonstrate_thread_safety() {
        auto node = std::make_shared<MyNode>();
        
        // Multiple threads can safely access parameters
        std::vector<std::thread> threads;
        
        // Thread 1: Setting parameters
        threads.emplace_back([node]() {
            for (int i = 0; i < 1000; ++i) {
                std::map<std::string, std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData>> params;
                params["key" + std::to_string(i)] = std::make_shared<StringData>("value" + std::to_string(i));
                node->setParam(std::move(params));
            }
        });
        
        // Thread 2: Reading parameters
        threads.emplace_back([node]() {
            for (int i = 0; i < 1000; ++i) {
                auto param = node->getParam("key" + std::to_string(i % 100));
                // Safe to access param even if it's null
                if (param) {
                    // Process parameter
                }
            }
        });
        
        // Thread 3: Managing successors
        threads.emplace_back([node]() {
            auto successor = std::make_shared<MyNode>();
            for (int i = 0; i < 1000; ++i) {
                node->next(successor, "action" + std::to_string(i % 10));
            }
        });
        
        // Wait for all threads to complete
        for (auto& thread : threads) {
            thread.join();
        }
    }
};
```

### FrameworkData Immutability

FrameworkData objects are designed to be immutable after construction, making them inherently thread-safe for read operations:

```cpp
#include "BaseNode/FrameworkData.h"

class ImmutableDataExample {
public:
    void demonstrate_immutable_data() {
        // Create shared data
        auto shared_data = std::make_shared<StringData>("shared value");
        
        // Multiple threads can safely read the same data
        std::vector<std::thread> readers;
        
        for (int i = 0; i < 10; ++i) {
            readers.emplace_back([shared_data, i]() {
                // Safe concurrent read access
                for (int j = 0; j < 1000; ++j) {
                    std::string value = shared_data->value;  // Thread-safe read
                    
                    // Type-safe casting is also thread-safe
                    if (auto* str_data = shared_data->as<StringData>()) {
                        std::cout << "Thread " << i << " read: " << str_data->value << std::endl;
                    }
                }
            });
        }
        
        for (auto& reader : readers) {
            reader.join();
        }
    }
};
```

### AsyncNode Execution Safety

AsyncNode prevents concurrent execution of the same node instance:

```cpp
#include "AsyncNode/AsyncNode.h"

class AsyncSafetyExample : public AsyncNode {
public:
    std::future<std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData>> ExecAsync(
        std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> prep_res) override {
        
        return std::async(std::launch::async, [prep_res]() {
            // This lambda runs in a separate thread
            // The AsyncNode ensures only one execution at a time per instance
            
            std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::seconds(1));
            
            if (auto* input = prep_res->as<StringData>()) {
                return std::static_pointer_cast<FrameworkData>(
                    std::make_shared<StringData>("Async processed: " + input->value)
                );
            }
            
            throw std::invalid_argument("Expected StringData");
        });
    }
};

void demonstrate_async_safety() {
    auto async_node = std::make_shared<AsyncSafetyExample>();
    auto input = std::make_shared<StringData>("test");
    
    // First execution starts
    auto future1 = async_node->RunAsync(input);
    
    try {
        // Second execution will throw because first is still running
        auto future2 = async_node->RunAsync(input);
        assert(false);  // Should not reach here
    } catch (const std::runtime_error& e) {
        std::cout << "Expected error: " << e.what() << std::endl;
        // "AsyncNode already executing - concurrent execution not allowed"
    }
    
    // Wait for first execution to complete
    auto result = future1.get();
    
    // Now second execution can proceed
    auto future3 = async_node->RunAsync(input);
    auto result2 = future3.get();
}
```

## Synchronization Primitives

### Shared Mutex for Reader-Writer Scenarios

The framework uses `std::shared_mutex` for scenarios with many readers and few writers:

```cpp
#include <shared_mutex>

class ReaderWriterNode : public BaseNode {
private:
    mutable std::shared_mutex data_mutex_;
    std::map<std::string, std::string> cached_data_;
    
public:
    // Multiple threads can read simultaneously
    std::string read_cached_data(const std::string& key) const {
        std::shared_lock<std::shared_mutex> lock(data_mutex_);
        
        auto it = cached_data_.find(key);
        return it != cached_data_.end() ? it->second : "";
    }
    
    // Only one thread can write at a time
    void write_cached_data(const std::string& key, const std::string& value) {
        std::unique_lock<std::shared_mutex> lock(data_mutex_);
        
        cached_data_[key] = value;
    }
    
    // Read-modify-write operation
    void update_cached_data(const std::string& key, 
                           std::function<std::string(const std::string&)> updater) {
        std::unique_lock<std::shared_mutex> lock(data_mutex_);
        
        auto it = cached_data_.find(key);
        std::string current_value = it != cached_data_.end() ? it->second : "";
        cached_data_[key] = updater(current_value);
    }
    
    // Bulk read operation
    std::map<std::string, std::string> read_all_cached_data() const {
        std::shared_lock<std::shared_mutex> lock(data_mutex_);
        
        return cached_data_;  // Copy while holding shared lock
    }
};
```

### Atomic Operations for Performance-Critical Code

```cpp
#include <atomic>

class AtomicCounterNode : public Node {
private:
    std::atomic<uint64_t> processed_count_{0};
    std::atomic<uint64_t> error_count_{0};
    std::atomic<uint64_t> total_processing_time_ns_{0};
    
public:
    std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> Execute(std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> shared) override {
        auto start_time = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
        
        try {
            auto result = Node::Execute(shared);
            
            // Atomic increment for success
            processed_count_.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
            
            auto end_time = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
            auto duration = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::nanoseconds>(
                end_time - start_time
            ).count();
            
            // Atomic add for timing
            total_processing_time_ns_.fetch_add(duration, std::memory_order_relaxed);
            
            return result;
            
        } catch (...) {
            // Atomic increment for errors
            error_count_.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
            throw;
        }
    }
    
    // Thread-safe statistics access
    struct Statistics {
        uint64_t processed_count;
        uint64_t error_count;
        double average_processing_time_ns;
        double success_rate;
    };
    
    Statistics get_statistics() const noexcept {
        Statistics stats;
        stats.processed_count = processed_count_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
        stats.error_count = error_count_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
        
        uint64_t total_operations = stats.processed_count + stats.error_count;
        if (total_operations > 0) {
            stats.success_rate = static_cast<double>(stats.processed_count) / total_operations;
            stats.average_processing_time_ns = static_cast<double>(
                total_processing_time_ns_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed)
            ) / stats.processed_count;
        } else {
            stats.success_rate = 0.0;
            stats.average_processing_time_ns = 0.0;
        }
        
        return stats;
    }
};
```

### Condition Variables for Coordination

```cpp
#include <condition_variable>
#include <queue>

template<typename T>
class ThreadSafeQueue {
private:
    mutable std::mutex mutex_;
    std::queue<T> queue_;
    std::condition_variable condition_;
    bool shutdown_ = false;
    
public:
    void push(T item) {
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(mutex_);
        
        if (shutdown_) {
            throw std::runtime_error("Queue is shut down");
        }
        
        queue_.push(std::move(item));
        condition_.notify_one();
    }
    
    bool pop(T& item, std::chrono::milliseconds timeout = std::chrono::milliseconds::max()) {
        std::unique_lock<std::mutex> lock(mutex_);
        
        bool success = condition_.wait_for(lock, timeout, [this] {
            return !queue_.empty() || shutdown_;
        });
        
        if (!success || (queue_.empty() && shutdown_)) {
            return false;
        }
        
        item = std::move(queue_.front());
        queue_.pop();
        return true;
    }
    
    void shutdown() {
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(mutex_);
        shutdown_ = true;
        condition_.notify_all();
    }
    
    size_t size() const {
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(mutex_);
        return queue_.size();
    }
    
    bool empty() const {
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(mutex_);
        return queue_.empty();
    }
};

class ProducerConsumerNode : public AsyncNode {
private:
    ThreadSafeQueue<std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData>> work_queue_;
    std::vector<std::thread> worker_threads_;
    std::atomic<bool> running_{true};
    
public:
    ProducerConsumerNode(size_t num_workers = std::thread::hardware_concurrency()) {
        // Start worker threads
        for (size_t i = 0; i < num_workers; ++i) {
            worker_threads_.emplace_back(&ProducerConsumerNode::worker_loop, this, i);
        }
    }
    
    ~ProducerConsumerNode() {
        // Shutdown workers
        running_ = false;
        work_queue_.shutdown();
        
        for (auto& worker : worker_threads_) {
            if (worker.joinable()) {
                worker.join();
            }
        }
    }
    
    std::future<std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData>> ExecAsync(
        std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> prep_res) override {
        
        auto promise = std::make_shared<std::promise<std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData>>>();
        auto future = promise->get_future();
        
        // Create work item
        auto work_item = std::make_shared<WorkItem>(prep_res, promise);
        
        // Add to queue
        work_queue_.push(work_item);
        
        return future;
    }
    
private:
    struct WorkItem : public FrameworkData {
        std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> data;
        std::shared_ptr<std::promise<std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData>>> promise;
        
        WorkItem(std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> d, 
                std::shared_ptr<std::promise<std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData>>> p)
            : data(std::move(d)), promise(std::move(p)) {}
        
        [[nodiscard]] std::unique_ptr<FrameworkData> clone() const override {
            return std::make_unique<WorkItem>(data->clone(), promise);
        }
        
        [[nodiscard]] const std::type_info& type() const noexcept override {
            return typeid(WorkItem);
        }
    };
    
    void worker_loop(size_t worker_id) {
        while (running_) {
            std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> work_data;
            
            if (work_queue_.pop(work_data, std::chrono::milliseconds(100))) {
                if (auto* work_item = work_data->as<WorkItem>()) {
                    try {
                        // Process the work item
                        auto result = process_work_item(work_item->data);
                        work_item->promise->set_value(result);
                    } catch (...) {
                        work_item->promise->set_exception(std::current_exception());
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
    
    std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> process_work_item(std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> data) {
        // Actual processing logic
        if (auto* input = data->as<StringData>()) {
            return std::make_shared<StringData>("Worker processed: " + input->value);
        }
        return data;
    }
};
```

## Async Programming Patterns

### Future-Based Composition

```cpp
#include <future>

class AsyncCompositionExample {
public:
    // Chain async operations
    std::future<std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData>> chain_async_operations(
        std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> input) {
        
        auto node1 = std::make_shared<AsyncProcessingNode>();
        auto node2 = std::make_shared<AsyncTransformNode>();
        auto node3 = std::make_shared<AsyncValidationNode>();
        
        // Chain operations using then-like pattern
        return node1->RunAsync(input)
            .then([node2](auto future) {
                auto result1 = future.get();
                return node2->RunAsync(result1);
            })
            .then([node3](auto future) {
                auto result2 = future.get();
                return node3->RunAsync(result2);
            });
    }
    
    // Parallel execution with synchronization
    std::future<std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData>> parallel_processing(
        std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> input) {
        
        auto node1 = std::make_shared<AsyncProcessingNode>();
        auto node2 = std::make_shared<AsyncProcessingNode>();
        auto node3 = std::make_shared<AsyncProcessingNode>();
        
        return std::async(std::launch::async, [=]() {
            // Start all operations in parallel
            auto future1 = node1->RunAsync(input);
            auto future2 = node2->RunAsync(input);
            auto future3 = node3->RunAsync(input);
            
            // Wait for all to complete
            auto result1 = future1.get();
            auto result2 = future2.get();
            auto result3 = future3.get();
            
            // Combine results
            return combine_results({result1, result2, result3});
        });
    }
    
private:
    std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> combine_results(
        const std::vector<std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData>>& results) {
        
        auto combined = std::make_shared<VectorData>();
        combined->data = results;
        return combined;
    }
};

// Extension to std::future for chaining (C++20 style)
template<typename T>
class ChainableFuture {
private:
    std::future<T> future_;
    
public:
    explicit ChainableFuture(std::future<T> future) : future_(std::move(future)) {}
    
    template<typename F>
    auto then(F&& func) -> ChainableFuture<std::invoke_result_t<F, std::future<T>&>> {
        using ReturnType = std::invoke_result_t<F, std::future<T>&>;
        
        auto promise = std::make_shared<std::promise<ReturnType>>();
        auto result_future = promise->get_future();
        
        std::thread([promise, func = std::forward<F>(func), future = std::move(future_)]() mutable {
            try {
                if constexpr (std::is_void_v<ReturnType>) {
                    func(future);
                    promise->set_value();
                } else {
                    auto result = func(future);
                    promise->set_value(std::move(result));
                }
            } catch (...) {
                promise->set_exception(std::current_exception());
            }
        }).detach();
        
        return ChainableFuture<ReturnType>(std::move(result_future));
    }
    
    T get() {
        return future_.get();
    }
    
    template<typename Rep, typename Period>
    std::future_status wait_for(const std::chrono::duration<Rep, Period>& timeout_duration) {
        return future_.wait_for(timeout_duration);
    }
};

template<typename T>
ChainableFuture<T> make_chainable(std::future<T> future) {
    return ChainableFuture<T>(std::move(future));
}
```

### Coroutine Support (C++20)

```cpp
#ifdef __cpp_impl_coroutine
#include <coroutine>

template<typename T>
class Task {
public:
    struct promise_type {
        T value_;
        std::exception_ptr exception_;
        
        Task get_return_object() {
            return Task{std::coroutine_handle<promise_type>::from_promise(*this)};
        }
        
        std::suspend_never initial_suspend() { return {}; }
        std::suspend_never final_suspend() noexcept { return {}; }
        
        void return_value(T value) {
            value_ = std::move(value);
        }
        
        void unhandled_exception() {
            exception_ = std::current_exception();
        }
    };
    
    using handle_type = std::coroutine_handle<promise_type>;
    
    explicit Task(handle_type handle) : handle_(handle) {}
    
    ~Task() {
        if (handle_) {
            handle_.destroy();
        }
    }
    
    Task(const Task&) = delete;
    Task& operator=(const Task&) = delete;
    
    Task(Task&& other) noexcept : handle_(std::exchange(other.handle_, {})) {}
    Task& operator=(Task&& other) noexcept {
        if (this != &other) {
            if (handle_) {
                handle_.destroy();
            }
            handle_ = std::exchange(other.handle_, {});
        }
        return *this;
    }
    
    T get() {
        if (!handle_) {
            throw std::runtime_error("Task is empty");
        }
        
        if (handle_.promise().exception_) {
            std::rethrow_exception(handle_.promise().exception_);
        }
        
        return std::move(handle_.promise().value_);
    }
    
    bool is_ready() const {
        return handle_ && handle_.done();
    }
    
private:
    handle_type handle_;
};

class CoroutineAsyncNode : public AsyncNode {
public:
    Task<std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData>> process_async_coroutine(
        std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> input) {
        
        // Simulate async work
        co_await std::suspend_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(100));
        
        if (auto* str_data = input->as<StringData>()) {
            auto result = std::make_shared<StringData>(
                "Coroutine processed: " + str_data->value
            );
            co_return std::static_pointer_cast<FrameworkData>(result);
        }
        
        throw std::invalid_argument("Expected StringData");
    }
    
    std::future<std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData>> ExecAsync(
        std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> prep_res) override {
        
        return std::async(std::launch::async, [this, prep_res]() {
            auto task = process_async_coroutine(prep_res);
            
            // Wait for coroutine to complete
            while (!task.is_ready()) {
                std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(1));
            }
            
            return task.get();
        });
    }
};

// Awaitable for framework data processing
struct FrameworkDataAwaitable {
    std::shared_ptr<AsyncNode> node;
    std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> input;
    
    bool await_ready() const { return false; }
    
    void await_suspend(std::coroutine_handle<> handle) {
        auto future = node->RunAsync(input);
        
        std::thread([future = std::move(future), handle]() mutable {
            try {
                auto result = future.get();
                handle.resume();
            } catch (...) {
                handle.resume();
            }
        }).detach();
    }
    
    std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> await_resume() {
        auto future = node->RunAsync(input);
        return future.get();
    }
};

Task<std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData>> process_pipeline_coroutine(
    std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> input) {
    
    auto node1 = std::make_shared<AsyncProcessingNode>();
    auto node2 = std::make_shared<AsyncTransformNode>();
    auto node3 = std::make_shared<AsyncValidationNode>();
    
    // Process through pipeline using coroutines
    auto result1 = co_await FrameworkDataAwaitable{node1, input};
    auto result2 = co_await FrameworkDataAwaitable{node2, result1};
    auto result3 = co_await FrameworkDataAwaitable{node3, result2};
    
    co_return result3;
}
#endif
```

## Cancellation and Timeouts

### CancellationToken Usage

```cpp
#include "BaseNode/CancellationToken.h"

class CancellableAsyncNode : public AsyncNode {
public:
    std::future<std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData>> RunAsyncWithCancellation(
        std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> shared,
        const CancellationToken& token) override {
        
        return std::async(std::launch::async, [this, shared, &token]() {
            return process_with_cancellation(shared, token);
        });
    }
    
private:
    std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> process_with_cancellation(
        std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> data,
        const CancellationToken& token) {
        
        // Long-running operation with cancellation checks
        for (int i = 0; i < 1000; ++i) {
            // Check for cancellation periodically
            token.throw_if_cancelled();
            
            // Simulate work
            std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(10));
            
            // Alternative: graceful cancellation check
            if (token.is_cancelled()) {
                std::cout << "Operation cancelled gracefully at step " << i << std::endl;
                return create_partial_result(data, i);
            }
        }
        
        return create_complete_result(data);
    }
    
    std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> create_partial_result(
        std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> input, int steps_completed) {
        
        if (auto* str_data = input->as<StringData>()) {
            return std::make_shared<StringData>(
                "Partial result (" + std::to_string(steps_completed) + " steps): " + str_data->value
            );
        }
        return input;
    }
    
    std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> create_complete_result(std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> input) {
        if (auto* str_data = input->as<StringData>()) {
            return std::make_shared<StringData>("Complete result: " + str_data->value);
        }
        return input;
    }
};

// Usage example
void demonstrate_cancellation() {
    auto node = std::make_shared<CancellableAsyncNode>();
    auto input = std::make_shared<StringData>("test data");
    
    CancellationToken token;
    
    // Start long-running operation
    auto future = node->RunAsyncWithCancellation(input, token);
    
    // Cancel after 2 seconds
    std::thread canceller([&token]() {
        std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::seconds(2));
        token.cancel();
        std::cout << "Cancellation requested" << std::endl;
    });
    
    try {
        auto result = future.get();
        std::cout << "Operation completed" << std::endl;
    } catch (const std::runtime_error& e) {
        std::cout << "Operation cancelled: " << e.what() << std::endl;
    }
    
    canceller.join();
}
```

### Timeout Policies

```cpp
#include "BaseNode/TimeoutPolicy.h"

class TimeoutAwareNode : public AsyncNode {
private:
    TimeoutPolicy default_policy_;
    
public:
    TimeoutAwareNode() {
        // Configure default timeout policy
        default_policy_.set_operation_timeout(std::chrono::seconds(30));
        default_policy_.set_retry_timeout(std::chrono::seconds(5));
        default_policy_.set_max_retries(3);
    }
    
    std::future<std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData>> RunAsyncWithPolicy(
        std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> shared,
        const TimeoutPolicy& policy) override {
        
        return std::async(std::launch::async, [this, shared, policy]() {
            return execute_with_timeout_policy(shared, policy);
        });
    }
    
private:
    std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> execute_with_timeout_policy(
        std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> data,
        const TimeoutPolicy& policy) {
        
        int retry_count = 0;
        
        while (retry_count <= policy.get_max_retries()) {
            try {
                // Execute with timeout
                auto future = std::async(std::launch::async, [this, data]() {
                    return perform_operation(data);
                });
                
                auto status = future.wait_for(policy.get_operation_timeout());
                
                if (status == std::future_status::ready) {
                    return future.get();  // Success
                } else {
                    // Timeout occurred
                    if (retry_count < policy.get_max_retries()) {
                        std::cout << "Operation timed out, retrying... (attempt " 
                                  << (retry_count + 1) << ")" << std::endl;
                        
                        // Wait before retry
                        std::this_thread::sleep_for(policy.get_retry_timeout());
                        retry_count++;
                        continue;
                    } else {
                        throw std::runtime_error("Operation timed out after " + 
                                               std::to_string(policy.get_max_retries()) + " retries");
                    }
                }
                
            } catch (const std::exception& e) {
                if (retry_count < policy.get_max_retries()) {
                    std::cout << "Operation failed, retrying... Error: " << e.what() << std::endl;
                    std::this_thread::sleep_for(policy.get_retry_timeout());
                    retry_count++;
                    continue;
                } else {
                    throw;  // Re-throw after max retries
                }
            }
        }
        
        throw std::runtime_error("Max retries exceeded");
    }
    
    std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> perform_operation(std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> data) {
        // Simulate potentially slow operation
        std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(
            std::rand() % 5000  // 0-5 seconds
        ));
        
        if (auto* str_data = data->as<StringData>()) {
            return std::make_shared<StringData>("Processed with timeout: " + str_data->value);
        }
        return data;
    }
};
```

## Lock-Free Programming

### Lock-Free Data Structures

```cpp
#include <atomic>

template<typename T>
class LockFreeStack {
private:
    struct Node {
        T data;
        std::atomic<Node*> next;
        
        Node(T d) : data(std::move(d)), next(nullptr) {}
    };
    
    std::atomic<Node*> head_{nullptr};
    
public:
    ~LockFreeStack() {
        while (Node* old_head = head_.load()) {
            head_ = old_head->next;
            delete old_head;
        }
    }
    
    void push(T item) {
        Node* new_node = new Node(std::move(item));
        Node* old_head = head_.load();
        
        do {
            new_node->next = old_head;
        } while (!head_.compare_exchange_weak(old_head, new_node));
    }
    
    bool pop(T& result) {
        Node* old_head = head_.load();
        
        while (old_head && !head_.compare_exchange_weak(old_head, old_head->next.load())) {
            // Retry if CAS failed
        }
        
        if (old_head) {
            result = std::move(old_head->data);
            delete old_head;
            return true;
        }
        
        return false;
    }
    
    bool empty() const {
        return head_.load() == nullptr;
    }
};

class LockFreeNode : public AsyncNode {
private:
    LockFreeStack<std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData>> pending_work_;
    std::atomic<bool> processing_{false};
    
public:
    std::future<std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData>> ExecAsync(
        std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> prep_res) override {
        
        // Add work to lock-free queue
        pending_work_.push(prep_res);
        
        return std::async(std::launch::async, [this]() {
            return process_pending_work();
        });
    }
    
private:
    std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> process_pending_work() {
        // Try to acquire processing lock atomically
        bool expected = false;
        if (!processing_.compare_exchange_strong(expected, true)) {
            // Another thread is already processing
            std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(1));
            return process_pending_work();  // Retry
        }
        
        std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> work_item;
        std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> result;
        
        if (pending_work_.pop(work_item)) {
            try {
                result = process_single_item(work_item);
            } catch (...) {
                processing_ = false;
                throw;
            }
        }
        
        processing_ = false;
        return result ? result : std::make_shared<StringData>("No work available");
    }
    
    std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> process_single_item(std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> item) {
        if (auto* str_data = item->as<StringData>()) {
            return std::make_shared<StringData>("Lock-free processed: " + str_data->value);
        }
        return item;
    }
};
```

### Memory Ordering Considerations

```cpp
class MemoryOrderingExample {
private:
    std::atomic<int> counter_{0};
    std::atomic<bool> flag_{false};
    std::atomic<std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData>> shared_data_{nullptr};
    
public:
    // Relaxed ordering for simple counters
    void increment_counter() {
        counter_.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    }
    
    int get_counter() const {
        return counter_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
    }
    
    // Acquire-release for synchronization
    void publish_data(std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> data) {
        shared_data_.store(data, std::memory_order_relaxed);
        flag_.store(true, std::memory_order_release);  // Release
    }
    
    std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> consume_data() {
        if (flag_.load(std::memory_order_acquire)) {  // Acquire
            return shared_data_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
        }
        return nullptr;
    }
    
    // Sequential consistency for critical operations
    bool try_lock_critical_section() {
        bool expected = false;
        return flag_.compare_exchange_strong(expected, true, std::memory_order_seq_cst);
    }
    
    void unlock_critical_section() {
        flag_.store(false, std::memory_order_seq_cst);
    }
};
```

## Common Pitfalls and Solutions

### Pitfall 1: Race Conditions in Lazy Initialization

```cpp
// ❌ Bad: Race condition
class BadLazyInit {
private:
    mutable std::shared_ptr<ExpensiveResource> resource_;
    
public:
    std::shared_ptr<ExpensiveResource> get_resource() const {
        if (!resource_) {  // Race condition here!
            resource_ = std::make_shared<ExpensiveResource>();
        }
        return resource_;
    }
};

// ✅ Good: Thread-safe lazy initialization
class GoodLazyInit {
private:
    mutable std::shared_ptr<ExpensiveResource> resource_;
    mutable std::once_flag init_flag_;
    
public:
    std::shared_ptr<ExpensiveResource> get_resource() const {
        std::call_once(init_flag_, [this]() {
            resource_ = std::make_shared<ExpensiveResource>();
        });
        return resource_;
    }
};
```

### Pitfall 2: Deadlock in Multiple Lock Acquisition

```cpp
// ❌ Bad: Potential deadlock
class BadMultipleLocks {
private:
    std::mutex mutex1_;
    std::mutex mutex2_;
    
public:
    void method1() {
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock1(mutex1_);
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock2(mutex2_);  // Potential deadlock
        // Do work
    }
    
    void method2() {
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock2(mutex2_);
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock1(mutex1_);  // Potential deadlock
        // Do work
    }
};

// ✅ Good: Ordered lock acquisition
class GoodMultipleLocks {
private:
    std::mutex mutex1_;
    std::mutex mutex2_;
    
public:
    void method1() {
        std::scoped_lock lock(mutex1_, mutex2_);  // Ordered acquisition
        // Do work
    }
    
    void method2() {
        std::scoped_lock lock(mutex1_, mutex2_);  // Same order
        // Do work
    }
};
```

### Pitfall 3: Exception Safety in Concurrent Code

```cpp
// ❌ Bad: Not exception safe
class BadExceptionSafety {
private:
    std::mutex mutex_;
    std::vector<std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData>> data_;
    
public:
    void add_data(std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> item) {
        mutex_.lock();
        data_.push_back(item);  // Exception here leaves mutex locked!
        mutex_.unlock();
    }
};

// ✅ Good: Exception safe with RAII
class GoodExceptionSafety {
private:
    std::mutex mutex_;
    std::vector<std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData>> data_;
    
public:
    void add_data(std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> item) {
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(mutex_);  // RAII ensures unlock
        data_.push_back(item);
    }
    
    // Even better: Strong exception safety
    void add_data_strong(std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> item) {
        std::vector<std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData>> temp_data;
        
        {
            std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(mutex_);
            temp_data = data_;  // Copy current state
        }
        
        temp_data.push_back(item);  // Modify copy (can throw)
        
        {
            std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(mutex_);
            data_ = std::move(temp_data);  // Commit (no-throw)
        }
    }
};
```

## Best Practices

### 1. Prefer Immutable Data

```cpp
// ✅ Good: Immutable data is inherently thread-safe
class ImmutableProcessingNode : public Node {
public:
    std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> Exec(std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> prep_res) override {
        // Create new data instead of modifying existing
        if (auto* input = prep_res->as<StringData>()) {
            return std::make_shared<StringData>("Processed: " + input->value);
        }
        return prep_res;
    }
};
```

### 2. Use RAII for Resource Management

```cpp
// ✅ Good: RAII ensures proper cleanup
class RAIINode : public AsyncNode {
private:
    class ResourceGuard {
        std::unique_ptr<Resource> resource_;
    public:
        explicit ResourceGuard(std::unique_ptr<Resource> r) : resource_(std::move(r)) {}
        ~ResourceGuard() { /* cleanup happens automatically */ }
        Resource* get() const { return resource_.get(); }
    };
    
public:
    std::future<std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData>> ExecAsync(
        std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> prep_res) override {
        
        return std::async(std::launch::async, [prep_res]() {
            ResourceGuard guard(std::make_unique<Resource>());
            
            // Use resource safely - cleanup is guaranteed
            return process_with_resource(prep_res, guard.get());
        });
    }
};
```

### 3. Minimize Lock Scope

```cpp
// ✅ Good: Minimal lock scope
class MinimalLockScope : public Node {
private:
    std::mutex data_mutex_;
    std::map<std::string, std::string> data_;
    
public:
    std::string get_and_process(const std::string& key) {
        std::string value;
        
        // Minimal lock scope for data access
        {
            std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(data_mutex_);
            auto it = data_.find(key);
            value = it != data_.end() ? it->second : "";
        }
        
        // Process outside of lock
        return expensive_processing(value);
    }
    
private:
    std::string expensive_processing(const std::string& input) {
        // Long-running operation without holding locks
        std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(100));
        return "Processed: " + input;
    }
};
```

### 4. Use Atomic Operations for Simple Cases

```cpp
// ✅ Good: Atomic operations for simple counters
class AtomicCounters {
private:
    std::atomic<uint64_t> success_count_{0};
    std::atomic<uint64_t> error_count_{0};
    
public:
    void record_success() {
        success_count_.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    }
    
    void record_error() {
        error_count_.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    }
    
    std::pair<uint64_t, uint64_t> get_counts() const {
        return {
            success_count_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed),
            error_count_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed)
        };
    }
};
```

### 5. Design for Composability

```cpp
// ✅ Good: Thread-safe composable operations
class ComposableAsyncNode : public AsyncNode {
public:
    // Composable async operations
    std::future<std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData>> compose_with(
        std::shared_ptr<AsyncNode> other,
        std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> input) {
        
        return RunAsync(input)
            .then([other](auto future) {
                auto intermediate = future.get();
                return other->RunAsync(intermediate);
            });
    }
    
    // Parallel composition
    std::future<std::vector<std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData>>> parallel_compose(
        const std::vector<std::shared_ptr<AsyncNode>>& nodes,
        std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> input) {
        
        return std::async(std::launch::async, [nodes, input]() {
            std::vector<std::future<std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData>>> futures;
            futures.reserve(nodes.size());
            
            // Start all operations
            for (auto& node : nodes) {
                futures.emplace_back(node->RunAsync(input));
            }
            
            // Collect results
            std::vector<std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData>> results;
            results.reserve(futures.size());
            
            for (auto& future : futures) {
                results.emplace_back(future.get());
            }
            
            return results;
        });
    }
};
```

This concurrency guide provides comprehensive coverage of thread safety, synchronization patterns, and best practices for building robust concurrent applications with the C++ Agentic Framework.

## Installation

### Prerequisites

- C++20 compatible compiler (GCC 10+, Clang 12+, MSVC 2019+)
- CMake 3.15 or higher
- Optional: Sanitizers for development (AddressSanitizer, ThreadSanitizer)

### Building the Framework

```bash
# Clone the repository
git clone <repository-url>
cd agentic-framework

# Create build directory
mkdir build && cd build

# Configure with CMake
cmake .. -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release

# Build
cmake --build . --parallel

# Run tests (optional)
ctest --parallel
```

### CMake Integration

Add to your `CMakeLists.txt`:

```cmake
# Find the framework
find_package(AgenticFramework REQUIRED)

# Link to your target
target_link_libraries(your_target 
    PRIVATE AgenticFramework::Core
)

# Enable C++20
target_compile_features(your_target PRIVATE cxx_std_20)
```

## Basic Concepts

### Core Components

The framework is built around several key concepts:

1. **FrameworkData**: Base class for all data types
2. **BaseNode**: Base class for all processing nodes
3. **Flow**: Orchestrates execution through connected nodes
4. **Result**: Type-safe error handling
5. **TypedData**: Type-safe data containers with validation

### Component Hierarchy

The framework provides a rich hierarchy of components for different use cases:

#### Node Types
- **Node**: Basic synchronous processing with retry capabilities
- **AsyncNode**: Asynchronous processing with futures, timeouts, and cancellation
- **BatchNode**: Synchronous batch processing for collections of data
- **AsyncBatchNode**: Asynchronous batch processing (non-blocking)
- **AsyncParallelBatchNode**: Parallel batch processing for maximum throughput

#### Flow Types
- **Flow**: Basic workflow orchestration with conditional routing
- **AsyncFlow**: Asynchronous workflow execution (non-blocking)
- **BatchFlow**: Workflow for batch data processing
- **AsyncBatchFlow**: Asynchronous batch workflow processing
- **AsyncParallelBatchFlow**: Maximum performance parallel batch workflows

#### Capability Matrix

| Component | Sync | Async | Batch | Parallel | Best For |
|-----------|------|-------|-------|----------|----------|
| **Node** | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | Simple processing |
| **AsyncNode** | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | Non-blocking operations |
| **BatchNode** | ✓ | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ | Large datasets |
| **AsyncBatchNode** | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | Non-blocking batches |
| **AsyncParallelBatchNode** | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | High-throughput processing |
| **Flow** | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | Simple workflows |
| **AsyncFlow** | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | Non-blocking workflows |
| **BatchFlow** | ✓ | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ | Batch workflows |
| **AsyncBatchFlow** | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | Non-blocking batch workflows |
| **AsyncParallelBatchFlow** | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | Maximum performance workflows |

### Data Flow Architecture

```
Input Data → Node 1 → Node 2 → Node 3 → Output Data
              ↓        ↓        ↓
           Parameters Parameters Parameters
```

Each node in the pipeline:
- Receives input data
- Processes it according to its logic
- Passes the result to the next node
- Can access configuration parameters
- Handles errors gracefully

## Your First Node

Let's create a simple text processing node:

### Step 1: Create a Custom Node

```cpp
#include "Node/Node.h"
#include "Flow/StringData.h"
#include <algorithm>
#include <cctype>

class TextProcessorNode : public Node {
public:
    // Constructor with retry configuration
    TextProcessorNode() : Node(3, 1000) {  // 3 retries, 1 second wait
        // Set default parameters
        std::map<std::string, std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData>> default_params;
        default_params["operation"] = std::make_shared<StringData>("uppercase");
        setParam(std::move(default_params));
    }
    
    std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> Exec(std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> prep_res) override {
        // Get the operation parameter
        auto operation_param = getParam("operation");
        std::string operation = "uppercase";  // default
        
        if (auto* op_data = operation_param->as<StringData>()) {
            operation = op_data->value;
        }
        
        // Process the input
        if (auto* input = prep_res->as<StringData>()) {
            std::string result = input->value;
            
            if (operation == "uppercase") {
                std::transform(result.begin(), result.end(), result.begin(), ::toupper);
            } else if (operation == "lowercase") {
                std::transform(result.begin(), result.end(), result.begin(), ::tolower);
            } else if (operation == "reverse") {
                std::reverse(result.begin(), result.end());
            } else {
                throw std::invalid_argument("Unknown operation: " + operation);
            }
            
            return std::make_shared<StringData>(result);
        }
        
        throw std::invalid_argument("Expected StringData input");
    }
    
    // Optional: Custom fallback for failed operations
    std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> exec_fallback(
        const std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData>& prep_res,
        std::exception_ptr eptr) const override {
        
        try {
            std::rethrow_exception(eptr);
        } catch (const std::exception& e) {
            std::cerr << "TextProcessor failed: " << e.what() << std::endl;
            // Return original input as fallback
            return prep_res;
        }
    }
};
```

### Step 2: Use Your Node

```cpp
#include "TextProcessorNode.h"

int main() {
    try {
        // Create the node
        auto processor = std::make_shared<TextProcessorNode>();
        
        // Configure the operation
        std::map<std::string, std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData>> params;
        params["operation"] = std::make_shared<StringData>("uppercase");
        processor->setParam(std::move(params));
        
        // Create input data
        auto input = std::make_shared<StringData>("hello world");
        
        // Process the data
        auto result = processor->Execute(input);
        
        // Extract the result
        if (auto* output = result->as<StringData>()) {
            std::cout << "Result: " << output->value << std::endl;  // "HELLO WORLD"
        }
        
    } catch (const std::exception& e) {
        std::cerr << "Error: " << e.what() << std::endl;
    }
    
    return 0;
}
```

## Common Usage Patterns

### Pattern 1: Sequential Processing Chain

```cpp
#include "Flow/Flow.h"

// Create multiple processing nodes
auto validator = std::make_shared<ValidationNode>();
auto transformer = std::make_shared<TextProcessorNode>();
auto logger = std::make_shared<LoggingNode>();

// Chain them together
validator->next(transformer);
transformer->next(logger);

// Create a flow
auto flow = std::make_shared<Flow>(validator);

// Process data through the entire chain
auto input = std::make_shared<StringData>("input data");
auto result = flow->orch(input);
```

### Pattern 2: Conditional Branching

```cpp
// Create nodes for different paths
auto validator = std::make_shared<ValidationNode>();
auto success_processor = std::make_shared<SuccessNode>();
auto error_handler = std::make_shared<ErrorHandlerNode>();
auto final_node = std::make_shared<FinalNode>();

// Set up conditional routing
validator->next(success_processor, "valid");
validator->next(error_handler, "invalid");

// Both paths converge at the final node
success_processor->next(final_node);
error_handler->next(final_node);

// The validator node determines the path based on its logic
class ValidationNode : public Node {
public:
    std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> Post(
        std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> shared,
        std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> prep_res,
        std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> exec_res) override {
        
        // Determine next action based on validation result
        if (auto* result = exec_res->as<StringData>()) {
            if (result->value == "valid") {
                // Flow will automatically route to "valid" successor
                return exec_res;
            }
        }
        
        // Default routing or error case
        return exec_res;
    }
};
```

### Pattern 3: Parallel Processing with Async Nodes

```cpp
#include "AsyncNode/AsyncNode.h"

class ParallelProcessorNode : public AsyncNode {
public:
    std::future<std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData>> ExecAsync(
        std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> prep_res) override {
        
        return std::async(std::launch::async, [prep_res]() {
            // CPU-intensive or I/O operation
            std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::seconds(1));
            
            if (auto* input = prep_res->as<StringData>()) {
                auto result = std::make_shared<StringData>(
                    "Processed in parallel: " + input->value
                );
                return std::static_pointer_cast<FrameworkData>(result);
            }
            return prep_res;
        });
    }
};

// Usage
auto async_node = std::make_shared<ParallelProcessorNode>();
auto input = std::make_shared<StringData>("data");

// Start async processing
auto future = async_node->RunAsync(input);

// Do other work while processing...
std::cout << "Processing in background..." << std::endl;

// Get the result when ready
auto result = future.get();
```

### Pattern 4: Batch Processing

```cpp
#include "BatchNode/BatchNode.h"
#include "BatchNode/VectorData.h"

class BatchTextProcessor : public BatchNode {
public:
    std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> exec(std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> items) override {
        auto* batch = items->as<VectorData>();
        if (!batch) {
            throw std::invalid_argument("Expected VectorData for batch processing");
        }
        
        auto result = std::make_shared<VectorData>();
        result->data.reserve(batch->data.size());  // Optimize memory allocation
        
        // Process each item
        for (const auto& item : batch->data) {
            if (auto* str_item = item->as<StringData>()) {
                auto processed = std::make_shared<StringData>(
                    "Batch: " + str_item->value
                );
                result->data.push_back(processed);
            }
        }
        
        return result;
    }
};

// Usage
auto batch_processor = std::make_shared<BatchTextProcessor>();

// Create batch data
auto batch = std::make_shared<VectorData>();
batch->data.push_back(std::make_shared<StringData>("item1"));
batch->data.push_back(std::make_shared<StringData>("item2"));
batch->data.push_back(std::make_shared<StringData>("item3"));

// Process the entire batch
auto result = batch_processor->Execute(batch);
```

### Pattern 5: Async Batch Processing

```cpp
#include "AsyncBatchNode/AsyncBatchNode.h"

class AsyncBatchProcessor : public AsyncBatchNode {
private:
    std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> exec(std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> items) override {
        auto* batch = items->as<VectorData>();
        if (!batch) {
            throw std::invalid_argument("Expected VectorData for async batch processing");
        }
        
        // Simulate async batch processing
        std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(100));
        
        auto result = std::make_shared<VectorData>();
        result->data.reserve(batch->data.size());
        
        for (const auto& item : batch->data) {
            if (auto* str_item = item->as<StringData>()) {
                result->data.push_back(
                    std::make_shared<StringData>("AsyncBatch: " + str_item->value)
                );
            }
        }
        
        return result;
    }
};

// Usage
auto async_batch_processor = std::make_shared<AsyncBatchProcessor>();
auto batch = std::make_shared<VectorData>();
// ... populate batch ...

// Process asynchronously
auto future = async_batch_processor->RunAsync(batch);
auto result = future.get();  // Non-blocking batch processing
```

### Pattern 6: Parallel Batch Processing

```cpp
#include "AsyncParallelBatchNode/AsyncParallelBatchNode.h"

class ParallelBatchProcessor : public AsyncParallelBatchNode {
private:
    std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> exec(std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> items) override {
        auto* batch = items->as<VectorData>();
        if (!batch) {
            throw std::invalid_argument("Expected VectorData for parallel batch processing");
        }
        
        // Process items in parallel using futures
        std::vector<std::future<std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData>>> futures;
        futures.reserve(batch->data.size());
        
        // Launch parallel processing tasks
        for (const auto& item : batch->data) {
            futures.emplace_back(
                std::async(std::launch::async, [item]() -> std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> {
                    if (auto* str_item = item->as<StringData>()) {
                        // Simulate CPU-intensive work
                        std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(50));
                        return std::make_shared<StringData>("Parallel: " + str_item->value);
                    }
                    return item;
                })
            );
        }
        
        // Collect results
        auto result = std::make_shared<VectorData>();
        result->data.reserve(futures.size());
        
        for (auto& future : futures) {
            result->data.push_back(future.get());
        }
        
        return result;
    }
};

// Usage for high-throughput scenarios
auto parallel_processor = std::make_shared<ParallelBatchProcessor>();
auto large_batch = std::make_shared<VectorData>();

// Create large batch
for (int i = 0; i < 1000; ++i) {
    large_batch->data.push_back(
        std::make_shared<StringData>("item_" + std::to_string(i))
    );
}

// Process with maximum parallelism
auto future = parallel_processor->RunAsync(large_batch);
auto result = future.get();  // All items processed in parallel
```

### Pattern 7: Advanced Flow Types

```cpp
#include "AsyncFlow/AsyncFlow.h"
#include "AsyncBatchFlow/AsyncBatchFlow.h"
#include "AsyncParallelBatchFlow/AsyncParallelBatchFlow.h"

// AsyncFlow - Non-blocking workflow execution
auto async_flow = std::make_shared<AsyncFlow>(start_node);
auto future = async_flow->RunAsync(input);

// AsyncBatchFlow - Non-blocking batch workflow
auto async_batch_flow = std::make_shared<AsyncBatchFlow>(batch_start_node);
auto batch_future = async_batch_flow->RunAsync(batch_input);

// AsyncParallelBatchFlow - Maximum performance workflow
auto parallel_flow = std::make_shared<AsyncParallelBatchFlow>(parallel_start_node);
auto parallel_future = parallel_flow->RunAsync(large_batch_input);

// All can be used with timeouts and cancellation
try {
    auto result = parallel_flow->RunAsyncWithTimeout(
        large_batch_input, 
        std::chrono::minutes(5)
    ).get();
} catch (const std::runtime_error& e) {
    std::cout << "Processing timed out" << std::endl;
}
```

## Working with Data

### Using TypedData for Type Safety

```cpp
#include "BaseNode/TypedData.h"

// Create typed data with validation
auto age = std::make_unique<TypedData<int>>(
    25,
    {Constraints<int>::range(0, 150)}  // Age must be 0-150
);

auto email = std::make_unique<TypedData<std::string>>(
    "user@example.com",
    {Constraints<std::string>::custom(
        [](const std::string& s) { return s.find('@') != std::string::npos; },
        "Must be a valid email address"
    )}
);

// Use in nodes
class UserProcessorNode : public Node {
public:
    std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> Exec(std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> prep_res) override {
        // Type-safe access
        if (auto* age_data = prep_res->as<TypedData<int>>()) {
            int age = age_data->get();
            
            if (age >= 18) {
                return std::make_shared<StringData>("adult");
            } else {
                return std::make_shared<StringData>("minor");
            }
        }
        
        throw std::invalid_argument("Expected age data");
    }
};
```

### Custom Data Types

```cpp
#include "BaseNode/FrameworkData.h"

// Define your custom data structure
struct UserData : public FrameworkData {
    std::string name;
    int age;
    std::vector<std::string> tags;
    
    UserData(std::string n, int a, std::vector<std::string> t)
        : name(std::move(n)), age(a), tags(std::move(t)) {}
    
    // Required FrameworkData interface
    [[nodiscard]] std::unique_ptr<FrameworkData> clone() const override {
        return std::make_unique<UserData>(name, age, tags);
    }
    
    [[nodiscard]] const std::type_info& type() const noexcept override {
        return typeid(UserData);
    }
    
    // Optional: Serialization support
    std::string serialize() const override {
        std::ostringstream oss;
        oss << name << "," << age << ",";
        for (size_t i = 0; i < tags.size(); ++i) {
            if (i > 0) oss << ";";
            oss << tags[i];
        }
        return oss.str();
    }
    
    bool deserialize(std::string_view data) override {
        // Implement deserialization logic
        // Return true on success, false on failure
        return false;  // Simplified for example
    }
};

// Use custom data in nodes
class UserProcessorNode : public Node {
public:
    std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> Exec(std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> prep_res) override {
        if (auto* user = prep_res->as<UserData>()) {
            // Process user data
            std::cout << "Processing user: " << user->name 
                      << " (age: " << user->age << ")" << std::endl;
            
            // Create result
            auto result = std::make_shared<StringData>(
                "Processed user: " + user->name
            );
            return result;
        }
        
        throw std::invalid_argument("Expected UserData");
    }
};
```

## Error Handling

### Using Result Types for Safe Operations

```cpp
#include "BaseNode/Result.h"

using namespace framework;

// Function that can fail
Result<std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData>> safe_divide(double a, double b) {
    if (b == 0.0) {
        return FrameworkError::invalid_argument("Division by zero");
    }
    
    auto result = std::make_shared<TypedData<double>>(a / b);
    return std::static_pointer_cast<FrameworkData>(result);
}

// Node using Result types
class SafeMathNode : public Node {
public:
    std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> Exec(std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> prep_res) override {
        // Chain operations with automatic error propagation
        auto result = extract_numbers(prep_res)
            .flat_map([](auto numbers) { return safe_divide(numbers.first, numbers.second); })
            .map([](auto data) {
                std::cout << "Division successful" << std::endl;
                return data;
            })
            .map_error([](const FrameworkError& e) {
                std::cerr << "Math operation failed: " << e.what() << std::endl;
                return e;
            });
        
        if (result.has_value()) {
            return result.value();
        } else {
            // Convert error to exception (or handle differently)
            throw result.error();
        }
    }
    
private:
    Result<std::pair<double, double>> extract_numbers(std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> data) {
        // Implementation to extract two numbers from input data
        // Return Result with pair of numbers or error
        return std::make_pair(10.0, 2.0);  // Simplified
    }
};
```

### Structured Error Handling

```cpp
#include "BaseNode/FrameworkError.h"

class RobustProcessorNode : public Node {
public:
    std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> Exec(std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> prep_res) override {
        try {
            return process_data(prep_res);
        } catch (const FrameworkError& e) {
            // Framework-specific error handling
            log_error("Framework error", e);
            throw;  // Re-throw or handle as appropriate
        } catch (const std::invalid_argument& e) {
            // Convert to framework error with context
            throw FrameworkError::invalid_argument(e.what(), "RobustProcessorNode::Exec");
        } catch (const std::exception& e) {
            // Generic error handling
            throw FrameworkError::runtime_error(e.what(), "RobustProcessorNode::Exec");
        }
    }
    
private:
    std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> process_data(std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> data) {
        // Your processing logic here
        if (!data) {
            throw FrameworkError::invalid_argument("Input data cannot be null");
        }
        
        // Process and return result
        return data;
    }
    
    void log_error(const std::string& category, const FrameworkError& error) {
        std::cerr << "[" << category << "] " 
                  << "Error in " << error.context() << ": " 
                  << error.what() << std::endl;
    }
};
```

## Async Operations

### Basic Async Processing

```cpp
#include "AsyncNode/AsyncNode.h"
#include "BaseNode/CancellationToken.h"

class AsyncDataFetcher : public AsyncNode {
public:
    std::future<std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData>> ExecAsync(
        std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> prep_res) override {
        
        return std::async(std::launch::async, [prep_res]() {
            // Simulate network request or file I/O
            std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::seconds(2));
            
            if (auto* url = prep_res->as<StringData>()) {
                // Simulate fetched data
                auto result = std::make_shared<StringData>(
                    "Data from: " + url->value
                );
                return std::static_pointer_cast<FrameworkData>(result);
            }
            
            throw std::invalid_argument("Expected URL string");
        });
    }
};

// Usage with timeout and cancellation
int main() {
    auto fetcher = std::make_shared<AsyncDataFetcher>();
    auto url = std::make_shared<StringData>("https://api.example.com/data");
    
    try {
        // With timeout
        auto future = fetcher->RunAsyncWithTimeout(
            url, 
            std::chrono::seconds(5)
        );
        auto result = future.get();
        std::cout << "Fetch completed" << std::endl;
        
    } catch (const std::runtime_error& e) {
        std::cerr << "Fetch timed out: " << e.what() << std::endl;
    }
    
    // With cancellation
    CancellationToken token;
    auto cancel_future = fetcher->RunAsyncWithCancellation(url, token);
    
    // Cancel after 1 second
    std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::seconds(1));
    token.cancel();
    
    try {
        auto result = cancel_future.get();
    } catch (const std::runtime_error& e) {
        std::cout << "Operation cancelled" << std::endl;
    }
    
    return 0;
}
```

### Async Flow Coordination

```cpp
#include "AsyncFlow/AsyncFlow.h"

class AsyncFlow : public Flow {
public:
    // Override to handle async nodes in the flow
    std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> orch(
        std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> shared,
        const std::map<std::string, std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData>>& params = {}) override {
        
        auto current_node = startNode;
        auto current_data = shared;
        
        while (current_node) {
            // Check if node is async
            if (auto* async_node = dynamic_cast<AsyncNode*>(current_node.get())) {
                // Handle async execution
                auto future = async_node->RunAsync(current_data);
                current_data = future.get();  // Wait for completion
            } else {
                // Handle sync execution
                current_data = current_node->Execute(current_data);
            }
            
            // Get next node (simplified)
            current_node = GetNextNode(current_node, "default");
        }
        
        return current_data;
    }
};
```

## Best Practices

### 1. Memory Management

```cpp
// ✅ Good: Use smart pointers
auto data = std::make_shared<StringData>("value");
auto node = std::make_shared<MyNode>();

// ❌ Bad: Raw pointers
StringData* data = new StringData("value");  // Memory leak risk
```

### 2. Exception Safety

```cpp
class SafeNode : public Node {
public:
    std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> Exec(std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> prep_res) override {
        // ✅ Good: RAII and exception safety
        std::unique_ptr<Resource> resource = acquire_resource();
        
        try {
            auto result = process_with_resource(prep_res, resource.get());
            return result;  // Resource automatically cleaned up
        } catch (...) {
            // Resource automatically cleaned up by unique_ptr
            throw;
        }
    }
};
```

### 3. Parameter Validation

```cpp
class ValidatingNode : public Node {
public:
    std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> Prep(std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> shared) override {
        // ✅ Good: Validate parameters early
        validateParams();
        
        auto required_param = getParamSafe("required_config");
        if (!required_param) {
            throw FrameworkError::invalid_argument(
                "Missing required parameter: required_config",
                "ValidatingNode::Prep"
            );
        }
        
        return shared;
    }
    
    void validateParams() const override {
        // Implement parameter validation logic
        auto timeout = getParam("timeout");
        if (timeout) {
            if (auto* timeout_data = timeout->as<TypedData<int>>()) {
                if (timeout_data->get() <= 0) {
                    throw FrameworkError::invalid_argument(
                        "Timeout must be positive",
                        "ValidatingNode::validateParams"
                    );
                }
            }
        }
    }
};
```

### 4. Resource Cleanup

```cpp
class ResourceManagedNode : public AsyncNode {
private:
    std::unique_ptr<ExpensiveResource> resource_;
    
public:
    ResourceManagedNode() : resource_(std::make_unique<ExpensiveResource>()) {}
    
    std::future<std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData>> ExecAsync(
        std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> prep_res) override {
        
        // Capture resource in lambda for safe async access
        auto resource_ptr = resource_.get();
        
        return std::async(std::launch::async, [prep_res, resource_ptr]() {
            // Use resource safely
            return resource_ptr->process(prep_res);
        });
    }
    
private:
    void cleanup_resources() noexcept override {
        // Custom cleanup if needed
        resource_.reset();
    }
};
```

### 5. Performance Optimization

```cpp
class OptimizedNode : public Node {
public:
    std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> Exec(std::shared_ptr<FrameworkData> prep_res) override {
        // ✅ Good: Reserve container capacity
        std::vector<std::string> results;
        results.reserve(expected_size);
        
        // ✅ Good: Use move semantics
        return std::make_shared<StringData>(std::move(processed_string));
    }
    
private:
    static constexpr size_t expected_size = 1000;
};
```

### 6. Thread Safety

```cpp
class ThreadSafeNode : public AsyncNode {
private:
    mutable std::shared_mutex data_mutex_;
    std::map<std::string, std::string> cached_data_;
    
public:
    std::string get_cached_value(const std::string& key) const {
        // ✅ Good: Shared lock for read operations
        std::shared_lock lock(data_mutex_);
        auto it = cached_data_.find(key);
        return it != cached_data_.end() ? it->second : "";
    }
    
    void set_cached_value(const std::string& key, const std::string& value) {
        // ✅ Good: Unique lock for write operations
        std::unique_lock lock(data_mutex_);
        cached_data_[key] = value;
    }
};
```

This getting started guide provides a comprehensive introduction to the C++ Agentic Framework with practical examples and best practices for building robust, efficient processing pipelines.

# Performance Tuning Guide

# Performance Tuning Guide
